quote_zh: Process Variant A): In a 1 I stirred apparatus, 100g of 2-chloro-3-methyl4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid were suspended in 400 ml of chlorobenzene. At room temperature, 85.9 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 6.6 g of azoisobutyroniltrile were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to 60° C. Afterwards, 2.6 g of bromine were added and the reaction mixture was further heated gradually to 90° C. The mixture was stirred at 90° C. for 2 h; after this time, HPLC analysis indicated a conversion of more than 98%. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 400 ml of water were added in succession and stirred well. The suspension was filtered, and the solid was washed and dried at 60° C. under reduced pressure. 121.3 g (88.4% of theory) of 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro4-methylsulfonyl-benzoic acid were obtained. Purity: 96% (HPLC) Melting point: 207-208° C.
arithmetic_check: IT CLOSES, EXACTLY, AND NOTHING IS FLAGGED. No mole figure is printed anywhere in this step, so there is no mass/mole pair to test and molar_mass_inconsistent cannot arise. Substrate: 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid is C9H9ClO4S, MW 9(12.011) + 9(1.008) + 35.453 + 4(15.999) + 32.06 = 248.68; 100 g is 0.40212 mol. Product: 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid is C9H8BrClO4S, MW 327.58, the substrate less one hydrogen plus one bromine (79.904 - 1.008 = 78.90, and 248.68 + 78.90 = 327.58). One bromine enters the side-chain methyl, so the transformation is one to one and the theoretical product is 0.40212 x 327.58 = 131.73 g. Stated isolate: 121.3 g at the stated 96% HPLC purity is 121.3 x 0.96 = 116.45 g of the named compound. Closure: 116.45 / 131.73 = 0.88400, i.e. 88.40% of theory, against the 88.4% printed at line 124. Agreement to three significant figures. Note that the crude 121.3 g uncorrected for purity would be 92.1% of theory, so the printed 88.4% is only reproducible once the printed 96% purity is applied, which is itself evidence that the two printed figures were computed against each other and against the correctly ordered methylsulfonyl structure rather than the as-printed sulfonylmethyl one. Reagent stoichiometry, checked for plausibility rather than flagged: 85.9 g of N-bromosuccinimide, MW 177.99, is 0.4826 mol, 1.20 equivalents against the substrate; 2.6 g of bromine, MW 159.81, is 0.0163 mol, 0.040 equivalents, consistent with the text's use of it as an accelerant alongside the N-bromosuccinimide rather than as the brominating charge; 6.6 g of azoisobutyronitrile, MW 164.21, is 0.0402 mol, 0.100 equivalents, a tenth of a mole of initiator per mole of substrate. Nothing is sub-stoichiometric in a way the text does not support and nothing exceeds what the substrate could consume. VERDICT: mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised, molar_mass_inconsistent is NOT raised, scale_discontinuity is NOT raised (no prior step feeds this one), and validation_flags is empty. Per A2 rule 29's second half, a step whose arithmetic closes gets no flag; inventing one here would be a false finding and would send a reviewer to a page where there is nothing to see.

quote_zh: Process Variant B): A 250 ml glass flask was initially charged with 5 g of 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid in 50 ml of methylene chloride and 50 ml of water. Under irradiation with a 300 W lamp, II g of bromine were gradually metered in over 3 h, and the mixture boiled under reflux. After a further 2 h of irradiation, the reaction mixture had been substantially decolorized. According to HPLC analysis, the reaction mixture contained 87% of product and 10% of reactant.
arithmetic_check: NOT CHECKABLE, AND THAT IS THE DOCUMENT RATHER THAN A DEFECT. Two of the three quantities a balance would need are simply not printed. Input: 5 g of C9H9ClO4S, MW 248.68, is 0.02011 mol, the one figure that is available. Brominating charge: line 130 prints 'II g of bromine', two capital-I letterforms and not the digits 11, verified on the pixels at 8x and restated nowhere in the document, so the bromine charge is unknown and is recorded with mass_g null. No number is substituted for it. For reference only, and NOT recorded on the artifact: were it 11 g, that would be 0.0688 mol of Br2, about 3.4 equivalents, which is a plausible photobromination charge, but plausibility is not evidence and the letterforms are what the page prints. Output: nothing is isolated. There is no product mass, no yield, no purity of an isolated solid and no melting point. The only outcome the step reports is an in-process HPLC composition of the reaction mixture, 87% product and 10% unconverted reactant, which is a composition and not a yield; converting it into one would require the mixture mass, which is not printed either. Step 1's 121.3 g and 88.4% belong to a different charge in a different vessel and are not carried across. So there is no stated product mass to test against the stated input moles and no stated mass/yield pair to test for internal agreement. VERDICT: mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised. The flag means the printed numbers contradict each other or exceed what the input could give; here the numbers are absent, and absence is not implausibility. Raising it would report a defect the patent does not contain and would mislabel a missing value as a wrong one. molar_mass_inconsistent is likewise not raised: no mass/mole pair is printed in this step at all. scale_discontinuity is not raised: this step's 5 g charge is an independent charge of purchased substrate, not material handed over from Step 1, because variants A and B are alternatives and no material flows between them. validation_flags is empty.
